c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: Hoary bats, solitary mammals that roost among tree leaves rather than in caves, migrate long distances each autumn. Tracking them is difficult, though: researchers attach radio tags weighing less than a gram to the bats' backs ______ even these lightweight devices, which are designed to fall off within weeks, rarely stay attached long enough to record a complete migration.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "researchers attach ... backs"와 빈칸 뒤 "even these lightweight devices ... rarely stay attached ..."는 각각 독립절이며, 뒤 절 안의 삽입구 "which are designed ... weeks"를 걷어내야 주어 devices와 동사 stay가 보인다. 두 독립절은 쉼표+등위접속사로 연결해야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론 뒤 but까지는 허용될 여지가 있지만 but과 even 사이의 쉼표가 불필요하게 접속사와 절을 끊는다. C는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 접속 오류(comma splice)이다. D는 아무 부호나 접속사 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("researchers attach ... backs") is an independent clause, and so is the text after it: once you set aside the nonessential clause "which are designed to fall off within weeks," you can see the subject "devices" and the verb "stay." Two independent clauses can be joined by a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B might look acceptable because a semicolon can come before "but," but the comma after "but" wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces. C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D fuses the two clauses with no punctuation or conjunction at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 절 안에 긴 비필수 관계절을 넣어 주절 구조를 가리고, 이미 쓰인 콜론 때문에 경계를 헷갈리게 했다. B는 세미콜론 부분은 그럴듯하지만 쉼표 위치가 틀린 오답으로 설계했다.

g.passage: In Wilhelmina Strand's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the widowed clerk Ezra Pell spends his evenings copying accounts by the light of a single candle, a habit his landlady considers both thrifty and faintly ______ the novel's quiet tension arises from her growing suspicion that the ledgers he copies belong to no business in town.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "In ... Ezra Pell spends ... sinister"까지의 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the novel's quiet tension arises ..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에는 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하며, 접속부사 indeed 뒤에는 쉼표를 둔다. B가 이 조건을 만족한다. A는 쉼표+and로 연결할 수 있어 보이지만 "and in fact," 뒤에 쉼표가 있고 in fact 앞의 쉼표가 없어 삽입구 처리가 맞지 않으며, 의미상으로도 B보다 어색하다. C는 접속부사 indeed를 쉼표로만 연결해 comma splice가 되고, D는 indeed를 sinister의 수식어처럼 붙여 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 역시 comma splice다.
g.explanation_en: Everything before the blank, ending with "sinister," is an independent clause, and "the novel's quiet tension arises..." is also a complete independent clause. Two independent clauses need a strong boundary, such as a semicolon, and the transition "indeed" should be followed by a comma, so B is correct. A tries to use a comma plus "and," but the phrase "in fact" isn't set off correctly (it has a comma after it but none before it), so the punctuation is unbalanced and the sentence reads awkwardly. C joins the two clauses with only commas around "indeed," which makes a comma splice, because "indeed" isn't a coordinating conjunction. D attaches "indeed" to "sinister" and still joins the clauses with just a comma, which is also a comma splice.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어(a habit his landlady considers...) 뒤에서 절 경계를 판단하게 하고, 접속부사 indeed와 쉼표+and 조합을 오답 함정으로 배치했다.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland in northern Botswana where a river fans out across the Kalahari Desert instead of reaching the sea, reaches its greatest extent in the dry winter months even though the region's rains fall in summer______ the floodwaters must travel slowly for several months from the highlands of Angola before they spread across the delta's channels and islands.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구를 걷어 내면 'The Okavango Delta ... reaches its greatest extent ... in summer'가 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the floodwaters must travel ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론을 써야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 등위접속사 'and'가 있지만 두 긴 독립절 사이에 필요한 쉼표가 없고, 'and'는 뒤 절이 앞 현상의 원인을 설명한다는 관계도 잘못 나타낸다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive, "The Okavango Delta ... reaches its greatest extent ... in summer" is a complete independent clause, and "the floodwaters must travel ..." after the blank is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. To join two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B uses the conjunction "and" but leaves out the comma needed between two long independent clauses, and "and" also misrepresents the relationship, since the second clause explains the cause of the first. D joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: Two decision steps: the student has to see past the long appositive and the "even though" clause to find the main clause, then recognize that what follows is a second independent clause. The distractors include a comma splice, "and" without a comma (which sounds plausible), and a run-on, so each must be compared with the others to rule it out.

g.passage: Founded in 1844 by a group of struggling weavers in Rochdale, England, the Rochdale Society of Equitable Pioneers adopted a set of principles that would later guide cooperative movements around the world ______ the store's members, rather than outside investors, controlled the business, and each member received a single vote no matter how many shares he or she owned.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'the Rochdale Society ... adopted a set of principles ...'라는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the store's members ... controlled the business, and each member received ...'도 독립절이며 앞에서 말한 원칙의 구체적 내용을 설명한다. 따라서 독립절을 연결하면서 앞 내용을 구체화하는 콜론을 쓴 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 연결한 콤마 스플라이스이다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 'that'이 붙어 뒤쪽이 독립절이 아닌 명사절 조각이 되므로 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "the Rochdale Society ... adopted a set of principles ...," is an independent clause. The text after it, "the store's members ... controlled the business, and each member received ...," is also an independent clause, and it spells out what those principles were. A colon joins two independent clauses when the second one explains or specifies the first, so D is correct. A creates a comma splice because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma. B creates a run-on sentence because it joins them with no punctuation at all. C adds "that," which turns the second part into a noun-clause fragment, and a semicolon can't come before a fragment.
g.design: The blank comes after a long introductory participial phrase and a relative clause, and the second clause contains an inserted "rather than" phrase. Because of this, students have to identify both independent clauses before choosing the colon. The semicolon choice in C looks plausible, but the word "that" turns the second part into a fragment.

g.passage: In the 1950s, engineers at the Tennessee Valley Authority faced a puzzle at the Fontana Dam, the tallest concrete dam east of the Rocky Mountains. Hairline cracks had begun appearing in its massive walls, and the cause, engineer Rhea Calloway and her team eventually concluded after years of monitoring______ the concrete itself was slowly expanding as a chemical reaction between its cement and certain minerals in the local aggregate produced a swelling gel.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "engineer Rhea Calloway ... after years of monitoring"는 주어 "the cause"와 동사 "was" 사이에 끼어든 삽입절이므로 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 그다음 "was surprising"으로 완전한 독립절이 끝나고, 뒤따르는 절은 그 원인을 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론이 알맞다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 삽입절은 바르게 닫지만, 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 생긴다. C는 뒤의 콜론은 맞지만 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 있다. D는 주어와 동사 사이에 세미콜론을 넣어 문장을 잘못 끊고, 끝도 쉼표 연결 오류가 된다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "engineer Rhea Calloway and her team eventually concluded after years of monitoring" interrupts the subject "the cause" and its verb "was." It opens with a comma, so it must close with a matching comma. After "was surprising," you have a complete independent clause, and the clause that follows explains what the cause was, so a colon fits. That makes A correct. B closes the interruption correctly, but it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C has the right colon but leaves out the comma that closes the interruption. D wrongly puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and it also ends in a comma splice.
g.design: I put a long interrupting clause between the subject and verb, so students have to make two decisions: close the interruption with a comma and pick the right boundary between the two clauses. B and C each get one of these decisions right, so students have to compare them carefully.

g.passage: Researchers studying the bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal whose populations appear to have reproduced without males for millions of years, expected its genome to show little variation______ they found that the tiny creature had incorporated thousands of genes borrowed from bacteria, fungi, and plants.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: A long appositive after the subject hides where the first independent clause ends, so students must first locate the two independent clauses and then see that the conjunctive adverb "instead" can't join them with only a comma.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Researchers ... expected its genome to show little variation"과 뒤 "they found that ..."은 각각 독립절이다. "instead"는 접속부사여서 등위접속사처럼 두 절을 이어 줄 수 없으므로, 앞에 세미콜론을 두고 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표로만 이어서 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. instead 양옆의 쉼표만 놓고 보면 A가 그럴듯해 보이지만 절 경계가 해결되지 않는다. C는 절 사이에 문장부호가 아예 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Researchers ... expected its genome to show little variation," is an independent clause, and so is the part after it, "they found that ...". "Instead" is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so it can't join two independent clauses on its own. That's why B is correct: a semicolon goes before "instead" and a comma goes after it. A and D link the two clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. A can look right because it sets off "instead" with commas on both sides, but it still doesn't mark the boundary between the clauses. C has no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

g.passage: In the opening chapter of Marisol Ventura's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, the widowed innkeeper Agnes Thorne reads aloud from her late husband's account book, a cracked volume bound in oxblood leather and stained with candle ______ each entry she recites reveals another debt he concealed from her during their twenty-two years of marriage.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격구가 있어 그 끝에서 독립절이 시작된다는 사실을 놓치기 쉽게 설계했다. 오답 B는 쉼표+등위접속사로 형식상 그럴듯하지만, 'and'가 동격구 안의 'bound ... and stained'와 병렬인 것처럼 잘못 연결되어 의미가 어색해지므로 문맥까지 따져야 배제된다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'Agnes Thorne reads aloud ...'라는 독립절이고, 'a cracked volume ... candle wax'는 account book에 대한 동격구이다. 빈칸 뒤 'each entry she recites reveals another debt ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 잇는 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 형식상 가능해 보이지만 'and'가 동격구 안의 'bound ... and stained' 병렬을 이어 가는 것처럼 읽혀, 단순한 첨가 관계가 되어 버리고 장부 낭독과 빚이 드러나는 내용 사이의 긴밀한 연결이 흐려진다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank is an independent clause ("Agnes Thorne reads aloud ..."), and "a cracked volume ... candle wax" is an appositive describing the account book. The part after the blank, "each entry she recites reveals another debt ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb, so C is correct because a semicolon properly joins two independent clauses. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B may look acceptable, but "and" reads as if it continues the "bound ... and stained" series inside the appositive, which turns the sentence into a loose list of additions and blurs the close link between reading the ledger and uncovering the debts. D joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland that spreads across northern Botswana, never empties into the sea______ floodwaters, which arrive from the Angolan highlands several months after the rainy season ends there, fan out across the Kalahari sands and either evaporate or sink into the ground.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The Okavango Delta ... never empties into the sea"와 빈칸 뒤 "its floodwaters ... fan out ... and either evaporate or sink"는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. B는 두 독립절 사이에 문장부호가 전혀 없어 run-on 문장이 된다. 동격구와 긴 which절에 들어간 쉼표들 때문에 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽다는 점에 주의해야 한다.

The wrong options show different misuses of punctuation around the conjunctive adverb "instead." g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Reformer James Kay ... documented the conditions ... in a widely read pamphlet"은 삽입구(a physician who ... 1832)를 포함하지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이며, 뒤의 "his detailed descriptions ... helped persuade officials ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 절을 부자연스럽게 끊는다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.

D joins the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, creating a run-on sentence.

g.passage: Aging water mains in many European cities lose a significant share of treated water through small cracks that worsen under high pressure. To address this problem, engineers in Lausanne, Switzerland, installed the PulseGuard valve—a palm-sized device that automatically lowers pressure in older pipes during low-demand nighttime hours______ in sixty neighborhoods, and over a two-year trial the system reduced leak-related losses by nearly 18 percent.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 'a palm-sized device ... hours'는 'the PulseGuard valve'를 설명하는 비필수 동격 삽입구이며, 대시로 시작했으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 '...installed the PulseGuard valve in sixty neighborhoods'라는 주절이 이어진다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 쉼표로 닫아 동격 앞뒤 부호가 일치하지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 필요한데 'in sixty neighborhoods'는 독립절이 아니다. D의 콜론은 삽입구를 닫지 못하며 'in sixty neighborhoods'를 앞 내용의 설명처럼 잘못 이어 준다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a palm-sized device ... nighttime hours" is a nonessential appositive describing "the PulseGuard valve." It opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash. Then the main clause continues: "installed the PulseGuard valve ... in sixty neighborhoods." That makes B correct. A closes the appositive with a comma, which doesn't match the opening dash. C uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on each side, but "in sixty neighborhoods" isn't one. D's colon doesn't close the interruption, and it wrongly presents "in sixty neighborhoods" as an explanation of what comes before it.
g.design: Readers have to notice the opening dash many words earlier and see that "in sixty neighborhoods" belongs to the main clause's verb, "installed." Students who skim may pick the comma or another boundary mark.

g.passage: Biologist Rosa Delgado spent three summers tracking the foraging routes of bumblebees in a Colorado mountain meadow. Her bees, each fitted with a tiny radio tag weighing less than a grain of rice, did not visit flowers at random______ they followed nearly identical circuits day after day, a behavior researchers call "traplining."
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her bees ... did not visit flowers at random"은 긴 삽입구(each fitted ... rice)를 포함하지만 주어 bees와 동사 did not visit을 갖춘 독립절이고, 뒤 "they followed nearly identical circuits..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하는 것이 적절하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 쉼표+등위접속사로 문법적 형식은 갖췄지만, and가 '무작위로 방문하지 않았다'와 '같은 경로를 따랐다'의 부연·대조 관계를 단순 추가로 만들고, 뒤 절이 앞 절을 설명하는 구조에 맞지 않는다. D는 which가 관계대명사로 뒤의 주어 they와 충돌해 문장이 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Her bees ... did not visit flowers at random," form an independent clause even though a long modifier (each fitted ... rice) sits inside it. The words after the blank, "they followed nearly identical circuits...," are also an independent clause. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B looks grammatical, but "and" just adds the second clause as a new fact. Here the second clause explains the first, so "and" misrepresents how the ideas relate. D uses "which" as a relative pronoun, and then the subject "they" has no grammatical place, so the sentence breaks down.
g.design: A long modifier separates the subject from its verb, so students have to recognize that the first part is still a complete independent clause. B is tempting because comma plus "and" is a form students learn to accept, so they have to check how the two ideas relate before ruling it out.

g.passage: The novelist Marguerite Thale, whose fog-bound harbor towns and candlelit drawing rooms deliberately recall the fiction of the 1850s, rarely names the decade in which her stories take place______ readers instead infer the period from small details, such as gaslit parlors, horse-drawn cabs, and letters sealed with wax.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 삽입절(whose ... 1850s)을 걸러 내면 주절은 "The novelist ... rarely names the decade..."로, 빈칸 앞은 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 "readers instead infer..." 역시 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로 두 절을 세미콜론으로 이은 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 등위접속사 and를 썼지만 긴 두 독립절을 이을 때 필요한 쉼표가 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long interrupting clause ("whose ... 1850s"), the main clause is "The novelist ... rarely names the decade...", which is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank, "readers instead infer...", is also an independent clause, so a semicolon correctly joins them, which makes D the answer. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. C uses the conjunction "and," but it leaves out the comma that's needed before a coordinating conjunction joining two long independent clauses.
g.design: The long nonrestrictive clause hides where the main clause starts and stops. Students have to find the main clause first and then choose the right boundary. Options A and C each look partly right (A has a comma, C has a conjunction), so they can only be ruled out by comparing them carefully.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland in northern Botswana where floodwaters spread across Kalahari sand instead of reaching the sea, floods at an unusual time of year______ its peak water levels arrive in the dry winter months, long after summer rains have fallen on the distant highlands of Angola.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격 수식어를 걷어내면 주절은 'The Okavango Delta ... floods at an unusual time of year'이고, 빈칸 뒤 'its peak water levels arrive...'도 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 '특이한 시기'를 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론을 쓴 A가 정답이다. Standard conventions don't use that combination, and it also hides the fact that the second clause explains the first.

g.passage: In 1840, the Great Western Railway began running its trains on London time rather than on the many local solar times kept by towns along its route. Railway time, as the new standard was soon called______spread beyond the stations themselves: by 1855, the great majority of public clocks in Britain had been reset to match it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 주어 'Railway time'과 동사 'spread' 사이에 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 삽입절이 있어, 여는 쉼표와 짝을 맞춰 닫는 문장부호를 골라야 한다. 대시·세미콜론 오답은 각각 삽입구 표지와 절 경계로 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.
g.explanation: 'as the new standard was soon called'는 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 삽입절이므로, 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어 'Railway time'과 동사 'spread'가 바르게 이어진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어+삽입절이라 독립절이 아니다. C는 삽입절을 닫지 않아 'called quickly spread'처럼 문장이 잘못 이어진다. D의 대시도 삽입 요소를 표시할 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입절을 대시로 닫으면 문장부호가 짝을 이루지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The clause "as the new standard was soon called" is a nonessential interruption that opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma as well. That way, the subject "Railway time" connects correctly to the verb "spread," which makes B the answer. A uses a semicolon, but a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the words before the blank are only a subject plus an interrupting clause, with no main verb. C leaves the interruption unclosed, so the sentence reads incorrectly as "called quickly spread." D uses a dash, which can mark an interruption, but an interruption that opens with a comma can't close with a dash because the punctuation has to match.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: Completed in 1997, the Maeslantkering protects Rotterdam from North Sea storm surges. The engineers who designed the barrier—a pair of hollow steel gates, each nearly as long as the Eiffel Tower is tall______ chose to store the gates in dry docks on opposite riverbanks, floating them into the waterway only when forecasters predict dangerously high water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "a pair of hollow steel gates ... tall"는 "the barrier"를 설명하는 동격어구로, 대시로 시작했으므로 끝도 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤에 주어 "The engineers"의 동사 "chose"가 온다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 쉼표는 동격어구를 끝내는 부호처럼 보이지만, 대시로 시작한 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫을 수는 없다. B의 세미콜론과 D의 콜론은 빈칸 앞이 이미 독립절인 것처럼 보이게 하지만, 실제로 빈칸 앞은 동사가 없는 주어부이므로 주어와 동사 "chose"를 부적절하게 갈라놓는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a pair of hollow steel gates ... tall" is an appositive describing "the barrier." Because it opens with a dash, it must also close with a dash, and after it comes "chose," the verb for the subject "The engineers." That makes C correct. A's comma might seem to end the appositive, but you can't close an interruption that opened with a dash using a comma. B's semicolon and D's colon treat the text before the blank as a complete independent clause. In fact, that text is a subject with no verb, so both choices wrongly separate the subject from its verb "chose."
g.design: This is a two-step problem. Students first have to find where the long appositive inside the dashes ends. Then they have to connect the subject to its distant verb. The comma and the semicolon/colon each look plausible on a quick read.

g.passage: Ecologist Mariana Velez spent three summers tracking the leafcutter ants of a Costa Rican cloud forest, a species whose foragers can carry fragments many times their own body weight. Her most surprising finding concerned the colony's waste workers, the older ants assigned to haul debris away from the fungus gardens ______ these workers, she discovered, almost never return to the nest's interior once they take up the job, a separation that likely keeps pathogens from spreading to the colony's food supply.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her most surprising finding concerned the colony's waste workers, the older ants assigned to haul debris away from the fungus gardens"는 동격 수식어로 끝나는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "these workers... almost never return..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표로 분리해야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 있다. 또한 바로 뒤 삽입구 "she discovered"의 쉼표와 겹쳐 문장 구조가 어색해진다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is a complete independent clause that happens to end with a long appositive phrase ("the older ants assigned to haul debris away from the fungus gardens"). After the blank, "these workers... almost never return..." is a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses need a proper boundary, so D, which uses a period, is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B does use the conjunction "and," but it puts an unnecessary comma after "and," and that comma clashes with the commas around the interrupting phrase "she discovered." C runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어가 첫 절 끝에 붙고 둘째 절에 삽입구가 있어, 훑어 읽으면 동격의 연장으로 착각해 쉼표(A)를 고르기 쉽게 설계했다.

g.passage: Edith Varne's novel The Salt Ledger, though written in 2019, borrows the brooding atmosphere of Victorian fiction. It opens at Marlow Fen, a crumbling manor whose east wing has been shut since the death of its first mistress______ on her first evening there, the new governess is warned never to climb past the second landing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격어구(a crumbling manor whose...)로 끝나지만 문장의 주절 "It opens at Marlow Fen"은 이미 완결되어 있고, 빈칸 뒤 "on her first evening there, the new governess is warned..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 잇는 세미콜론을 쓴 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 which가 관계절을 시작하지만, 뒤에 이미 주어 the new governess가 있어 관계사가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The long appositive (a crumbling manor whose east wing...) comes after a complete main clause, "It opens at Marlow Fen." The text after the blank, "on her first evening there, the new governess is warned...," is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so A is right. B joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C joins them with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on. D starts a relative clause with "which," but that clause already has a subject ("the new governess"), so "which" has no role to play and the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어 뒤에 독립절이 새로 시작되고 그 앞에 도입 전치사구가 붙어 있다. 그래서 훑어 읽으면 쉼표로 이어도 되는 수식어처럼 보이게 설계했다.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland in northern Botswana, never reaches the sea. Instead, the floodwaters that arrive each year from the Angolan highlands spread across the flat sands of the Kalahari Basin and slowly ______ more than 95 percent of the water is lost to evaporation and plant transpiration before it can drain away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the floodwaters ... slowly disappear"와 뒤 "more than 95 percent of the water is lost ..."는 각각 독립절이며, 뒤 절이 물이 사라지는 방식을 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결한 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. C는 관계대명사 which가 뒤 절에서 아무 역할도 하지 않아 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("the floodwaters ... slowly disappear") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("more than 95 percent of the water is lost ..."). The second clause explains how the water disappears, so a colon is the right way to join them. That makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C adds "which," but "which" plays no role in the clause that follows, so the sentence is ungrammatical. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all.
g.design: The subject and verb of the first clause are separated by long modifiers, and a passive second clause follows, so students have to see that both sides are independent clauses (rule) and that the second one explains the first (context). The "which" distractor looks natural when skimmed.

g.passage: In 1871, Maejima Hisoka, a former government official who had studied the British postal service, launched Japan's first state-run mail route between Tokyo and Osaka. Within a decade, the network had reached most of the country's towns, and its effects extended well beyond letter delivery______ post offices began accepting small deposits, giving millions of rural households their first access to a formal savings account.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "its effects extended well beyond letter delivery"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "post offices began accepting small deposits..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며 앞 내용의 구체적 예시를 제시한다. 콜론은 독립절 뒤에서 이를 설명하거나 구체화하는 내용을 이끌 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 아무 문장부호 없이 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 comma splice가 된다. D는 "which"가 관계사로 쓰였지만 뒤 절에 이미 주어와 목적어가 다 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "its effects extended well beyond letter delivery," is an independent clause. The text after it, "post offices began accepting small deposits...," is also an independent clause, and it gives a specific example of those wider effects. A colon can follow an independent clause to introduce an explanation or example, so C is correct. A runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation, which creates a run-on sentence. B joins them with only a comma, which is a comma splice. D adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own subject and object, so it can't work as a relative clause.
g.design: 독립절 앞뒤 경계를 판단하되 앞부분에 동격 삽입구와 등위절을 두어 문장 구조를 복잡하게 했다. 쉼표·관계사 오답은 겉보기에 자연스러워 보이게 만들었다.

g.passage: Tuned mass dampers, heavy weights mounted on springs so that they sway out of step with the structure they protect, are usually associated with skyscrapers. In a 2019 retrofit, however, engineers attached six compact dampers beneath a steel footbridge whose deck had bounced noticeably under groups of joggers ______ dropped by nearly 80 percent in follow-up tests.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞에는 "engineers attached ... joggers"라는 독립절이 있고, 그 안에 긴 수식어(whose deck ...)가 들어 있다. 빈칸 뒤에도 "the deck's vertical oscillations dropped"라는 독립절이 온다. 두 독립절은 쉼표+등위접속사로 연결해야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 대시와 and로 시작하는 연결은 가능해 보이지만, 주어 oscillations와 동사 dropped 사이에 쉼표가 들어가 틀렸다. C는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙여 쓰는데, 이는 표준 용법이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank you have a complete independent clause, "engineers attached ... joggers," and a long modifier sits inside it. After the blank comes a second independent clause, "the deck's vertical oscillations dropped...." Two independent clauses can be joined with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B looks like it could work because it uses a dash with "and," but it puts a comma between the subject "oscillations" and its verb "dropped." C puts a colon right before the conjunction "and," and that isn't standard usage.
g.design: This is a clause-boundary question that comes after a long relative-clause modifier. Every wrong choice has a plausible piece (a comma, a conjunction, a strong mark), so you have to compare them closely to rule them out.

g.passage: The bigclaw snapping shrimp, a crustacean barely five centimeters long that lives among coral rubble and seagrass, hunts in an unusual way______ it creates a jet of water so fast that a collapsing bubble briefly stuns nearby fish and worms.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: : by snapping its oversized claw shut,
, by snapping its oversized claw shut,
by snapping its oversized claw shut,
g.explanation: 지문에는 독립절이 두 개 있다. 'The bigclaw snapping shrimp ... hunts in an unusual way'와 'it creates a jet ...'이다. 'by snapping its oversized claw shut'은 두 번째 절에 속하는 수식어구다. 따라서 두 절 사이에는 콜론처럼 절과 절을 연결할 수 있는 경계가 필요하며, 콜론 뒤 절은 앞에서 말한 '특이한 방식'을 설명한다. 그러므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 대시 두 개가 수식어구를 삽입구로 묶는데, 이를 빼면 'way it creates'만 남아 두 절이 아무 연결 없이 붙은 무종지문이 된다. D는 경계 표시가 전혀 없어 마찬가지로 무종지문이다.
g.explanation_en: The passage contains two independent clauses: "The bigclaw snapping shrimp ... hunts in an unusual way" and "it creates a jet ...". The phrase "by snapping its oversized claw shut" is a modifier that belongs to the second clause. So you need a mark that can join two clauses, such as a colon, and here the second clause explains the "unusual way." That makes A correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts the modifier between dashes as an interruption, but if you remove it, you get "way it creates," which joins two clauses with no connection at all and makes a run-on sentence. D has no boundary punctuation at all, so it is also a run-on sentence.
g.design: I placed a long appositive after the subject, then put the introductory modifier of the second clause inside the blank. You have to recognize where the clause boundary falls. Choices B and C look plausible because their punctuation seems to fit the modifier, but they don't handle the boundary between the two clauses.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: In Hollis Wren's novel The Lamplighter's Ledger, set in a fog-bound port town, the widowed bookkeeper Margery Thrale keeps two sets of accounts: one for the shipping firm that employs her and one, written in a private cipher, recording the debts the townspeople owe one another in kindness and cruelty. The second ledger, which she hides beneath a loose floorboard in her ______ the novel's true subject, for every chapter turns on an entry Margery has made in it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The second ledger"이고 동사는 "is"이며, 그 사이에 비필수 관계절 "which she hides beneath a loose floorboard in her attic"이 삽입되어 있다. 비필수 관계절은 앞뒤를 쉼표로 감싸야 하므로 "attic" 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하고, 동사 "is"와 보어 "the novel's true subject" 사이에는 문장부호가 없어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 관계절을 올바르게 닫지만 동사와 보어 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다. C는 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 "which" 앞의 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 세미콜론을 써서 주어와 동사를 갈라놓으므로 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The second ledger" and its verb is "is." Between them sits a nonessential relative clause: "which she hides beneath a loose floorboard in her attic." A nonessential clause needs a comma on both sides, so you need a comma after "attic," and you shouldn't put any punctuation between "is" and its complement, "the novel's true subject." That makes B correct. A closes the clause correctly but adds an unnecessary comma between the verb and its complement. C leaves out the comma that closes the clause, so the comma before "which" has no partner. D puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, so the part before the semicolon isn't an independent clause.
g.design: The long nonessential relative clause between the subject and verb hides the sentence's main structure, and the "for" clause later in the sentence may make a clause boundary at the blank seem likely. A, which adds an extra comma after the verb, and C, which leaves out the closing comma, are each partly correct, so you have to compare them carefully to rule them out.

g.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, the Sundarbans mangrove forest acts as a living barrier against cyclones. Geographer Rahim Chowdhury, who has mapped shoreline change in the region for two decades, found that villages sheltered by at least a kilometer of dense mangroves suffered far less storm-surge damage than exposed villages ______ the roots and trunks of the trees slow incoming water, reducing both its height and its force before it reaches inland settlements.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸에는 독립절 두 개("villages ... did"와 "The explanation is simple")를 구분하는 경계와, "simple" 뒤에서 그 설명을 이어 주는 경계가 필요하다. C는 마침표로 두 독립절을 분리하고, 콜론으로 앞 절을 구체적으로 설명하는 독립절을 도입하므로 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절 세 개를 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 생긴다. B는 콜론은 맞게 썼지만 "did" 뒤 쉼표가 두 독립절을 잘못 연결한다. D는 세미콜론으로 첫 경계는 맞게 처리했지만 "simple" 뒤 쉼표가 독립절 두 개를 잘못 연결한다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs two boundaries: one between the independent clauses "villages ... did" and "The explanation is simple," and another after "simple" to introduce the clause that explains it. C is correct because the period separates the first two independent clauses, and the colon introduces an independent clause that spells out the explanation. A joins three independent clauses with commas alone, so it creates comma splices. B uses the colon correctly, but the comma after "did" still splices two independent clauses together. D handles the first boundary correctly with a semicolon, but the comma after "simple" joins two independent clauses incorrectly.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구와 비교 구문 뒤에서 절 경계 두 곳을 모두 판단해야 한다. B와 D는 각각 경계 하나만 맞게 처리하는 부분 정답으로 설계했다.

g.passage: In the 1840s, the Lowell Female Labor Reform Association, a group of New England textile workers led by mill operative Sarah Bagley, gathered thousands of signatures on petitions demanding a ten-hour workday. Although the Massachusetts legislature declined to pass such a law, the campaign had a lasting effect on the ______ the first time, many legislators heard factory women testify publicly about conditions inside the mills.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 종속절 뒤 독립절이 끝나는 지점을 찾아야 하며, 'for'가 접속사처럼 보이는 함정과 'and'가 문맥상 설명 관계를 흐리는 함정을 두어 문법+문맥 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the campaign had a lasting effect on the state's political debate'는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 'for the first time, many legislators heard...'도 독립절로서 앞의 '지속적 영향'을 구체적으로 설명한다. 두 독립절을 잇고 뒤 절이 앞 절을 부연할 때는 콜론이 적절하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표+for를 등위접속사 'for(왜냐하면)'로 읽으면 문법적으로 가능해 보이지만, 그러면 'for'가 'for the first time'의 전치사 역할을 동시에 할 수 없어 뒤 절이 'the first time, many legislators...'라는 깨진 구조가 된다. B는 두 독립절을 아무 부호 없이 이어 run-on 문장이 되고, C는 문법상 연결은 되지만 'and'가 뒤 절을 앞 절의 설명이 아닌 별개의 추가 사실로 만들어 문맥 관계를 흐린다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "the campaign had a lasting effect on the state's political debate," is a complete independent clause. What follows, "for the first time, many legislators heard...," is also an independent clause, and it explains what that lasting effect was. When a second independent clause explains or elaborates on the first, a colon is the right choice, so D is correct. A looks possible if you read "for" as the coordinating conjunction meaning "because," but "for" can't also work as the preposition in "for the first time," so the second clause would be left as the broken "the first time, many legislators...". B joins the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. C is grammatically acceptable, but "and" makes the second clause sound like a separate added fact rather than an explanation of the first, so it blurs the logical relationship between the clauses.

g.passage: In 1959, engineers at the Dutch firm Philips faced a puzzle: their new compact cassette needed to be small enough for a coat pocket yet durable enough to survive years of handling. Lou Ottens, the project's lead ______ this constraint by first carving a prototype from a block of wood that fit inside his jacket, then insisting that every later design match its dimensions.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "the project's lead engineer"는 주어 Lou Ottens를 설명하는 비필수 동격어구이므로 앞뒤로 쉼표를 짝지어 써야 하고, 그 뒤에 동사 addressed가 이어져야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 동격어구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 앞의 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 주어 없는 동사구만 남아 독립절이 되지 못한다. D는 and가 주어와 동사 사이를 끊어, 주어 Lou Ottens가 본동사를 갖지 못하게 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "the project's lead engineer" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, Lou Ottens, so it must be set off by a pair of commas, followed by the verb "addressed." That makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so the comma before the appositive has no partner. C puts a semicolon before a verb phrase that has no subject, so what follows can't stand as an independent clause. D inserts "and" between the subject and its verb, which leaves "Lou Ottens" without a main verb.
g.design: 이 문항은 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 동격어구를 넣고, 앞쪽 쉼표만 지문에 보이게 했다. 학생은 이 쉼표의 짝을 찾는 규칙을 적용하고, 문장의 주어-동사 구조도 확인하는 두 단계 판단을 해야 한다. 오답 C와 D는 그럴듯한 연결처럼 보이도록 만들었다.

g.passage: Biologist Mariana Okafor studies the Pacific chorus frog, a small amphibian whose skin can shift from green to brown over a period of several weeks______ field surveys by her team suggest that this change tracks seasonal shifts in the color of surrounding vegetation rather than changes in air temperature.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'Biologist Mariana Okafor studies the Pacific chorus frog'라는 독립절에 긴 동격어구가 붙은 형태이고, 빈칸 뒤 'field surveys ... suggest ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 있다. C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank is an independent clause, "Biologist Mariana Okafor studies the Pacific chorus frog," followed by a long appositive. After the blank is another independent clause, "field surveys by her team suggest...," which has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses the coordinating conjunction "and," which is a reasonable choice, but it adds an unnecessary comma after "and." C joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: The long appositive hides where the first independent clause ends, so students have to find both clauses before choosing how to join them. Option A uses a correct conjunction but adds an extra comma, which makes it a tempting wrong answer.

g.passage: Each evening the widow Marchbank, who had lived alone at Fernhollow for eleven winters and who, the villagers believed, had long since forgotten the sound of another voice______ two cups upon the table, as though a guest were expected at any moment.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 관계절과 삽입구(the villagers believed)가 끼어 있어, 수식어를 닫는 문장부호가 앞의 여는 쉼표와 짝을 이뤄야 함을 파악하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 대시와 세미콜론은 그럴듯해 보이지만 짝이 맞지 않거나 주어와 동사를 갈라놓는다.
g.explanation: 주어 "the widow Marchbank" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작하는 비필수 관계절(who had lived ... another voice)이 이어지므로, 동사 "set" 앞에서도 쉼표로 수식어를 닫아야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 독립절 사이에만 쓰이는데, 이 문장은 주어와 동사 "set"을 갈라 놓게 된다. B의 대시도 수식어를 닫을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입은 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 앞의 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 관계절이 끝나는 지점이 표시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "the widow Marchbank" is followed by a nonessential relative clause that opens with a comma (who had lived ... another voice). That clause must also be closed with a comma before the main verb "set," so C is correct. A uses a semicolon, which belongs only between independent clauses, so here it would cut the subject off from its verb "set." B uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but an interruption opened with a comma has to be closed with a comma, so the dash doesn't match. D leaves out the closing punctuation, so nothing marks where the relative clause ends.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta, an inland wetland in northern Botswana that floods each year during the region's dry season, receives most of its water from rains that fall hundreds of kilometers away in the Angolan highlands______ rains take several months to travel downstream, so the delta swells just as the surrounding savanna reaches its driest point.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구(an inland wetland ... dry season)를 걷어내면 주절은 'The Okavango Delta ... receives most of its water ... highlands'이고, 빈칸 뒤 'those rains take several months ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 붙여 콜론의 쓰임에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive (an inland wetland ... dry season), the main clause is "The Okavango Delta ... receives most of its water ... highlands." The text after the blank, "those rains take several months ...," is also an independent clause because it has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A creates a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. B fuses the clauses with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence. C puts the conjunction "and" after a colon, and that isn't how a colon is used.
g.design: A long appositive and a relative clause separate the subject from its verb, so students have to find the main clause before they can see that the blank falls between two independent clauses. The wrong answers are a comma splice, a run-on, and a colon followed by a conjunction.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

g.passage: Before the 1890s, most American farm families had to travel to a distant town, sometimes only once a week, to collect their mail. The introduction of Rural Free Delivery, a federal program that brought letters and parcels directly to farmhouse ______ transformed rural life: mail-order catalogs, daily newspapers, and political pamphlets suddenly reached households that had long been cut off from national events.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The introduction of Rural Free Delivery"이고 동사는 "transformed"이다. 사이에 있는 "a federal program ... farmhouse doors"는 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 동격 표현이다. 따라서 이 동격을 같은 부호인 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분을 독립절이 아니게 만든다. C는 동격을 닫는 부호가 없어 "doors"가 "transformed"의 주어처럼 읽힌다. D의 대시는 동격 표현을 끝맺을 수 있는 부호이지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫을 수는 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The introduction of Rural Free Delivery," and its verb is "transformed." Between them is a nonessential appositive, "a federal program ... farmhouse doors," and it opens with a comma. You need the same mark to close it, so A is correct. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, so the part before the semicolon isn't an independent clause. C has no closing punctuation, so "doors" reads as if it were the subject of "transformed." D's dash could end an appositive, but you can't close a phrase with a dash when it was opened with a comma.
g.design: The blank comes after a long appositive that sits between the subject and the verb. To answer, students first find the comma that opens the appositive and then match the closing mark to it. Options B and D look plausible to someone reading quickly, because the colon later in the sentence makes other punctuation seem possible.

g.passage: In 1998, engineers in Hong Kong faced a problem when building the Tsing Ma Bridge's companion structures: typhoon winds could twist a long deck until it failed. Their solution, borrowed from aircraft design, was a hollow deck shaped like a flattened wing, with slotted vents running along its center. The vents, which let gusts pass through the deck rather than push against ______ the pressure difference between the upper and lower surfaces, keeping the span steady even in winds above 200 kilometers per hour.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 "The vents" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비제한 관계절 "which let gusts ... push against it"가 삽입되어 있으므로, 이 절을 닫는 쉼표가 필요하고 그 뒤에 본동사 "reduce"가 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 "and"가 들어가 "reduce"가 관계절 안의 동사와 병렬이 되어 주절에 본동사가 사라진다. D는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 없어 여는 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The vents" is interrupted by a nonrestrictive clause that opens with a comma ("which let gusts ... push against it"), so a second comma must close that clause before the main verb "reduce." That makes B correct. A puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, so the part before the semicolon isn't an independent clause. C adds "and," which makes "reduce" parallel with the verbs inside the relative clause and leaves the main clause with no verb. D leaves out the closing comma, so the comma that opens the interrupting clause has no partner.
g.design: 긴 비제한 관계절이 주어와 본동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 독자는 절의 경계를 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. 먼저 쉼표가 짝을 이루는지 확인하고, 그다음 본동사가 남아 있는지 확인한다. 세미콜론과 "and"를 넣은 오답은 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보인다.

g.passage: In the cloud forests of Costa Rica, ecologist Mariela Fonseca tracked how resplendent quetzals disperse the seeds of wild avocado trees. The birds swallow the fruits whole and later regurgitate the large pits, often far from the parent tree. The seedlings that sprout from these scattered pits, unlike those growing directly beneath an adult avocado where fungal pathogens accumulate in the soil, ______ markedly higher survival rates over their first two years.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "The seedlings"이며, "that sprout from these scattered pits" 관계절과 "unlike ... in the soil" 삽입구는 주어를 수식할 뿐 문장의 정동사가 아니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 C "show"가 정답이다. A "having shown"과 D "to show"는 분사·부정사여서 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다. B "shows"는 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "an adult avocado"나 "soil"에 맞춘 단수형이라 복수 주어 "seedlings"와 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The seedlings." The relative clause "that sprout from these scattered pits" and the phrase "unlike ... in the soil" only modify that subject; neither one is the sentence's main verb. So the blank needs a main verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes C, "show," correct. A ("having shown") is a participle and D ("to show") is an infinitive, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb. B ("shows") is singular. It seems to fit the nearby singular nouns "an adult avocado" or "soil," but it doesn't agree with the plural subject "seedlings."
g.design: 긴 관계절과 삽입된 비교구로 주어와 빈칸을 떼어 놓고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 단수 명사를 두어 단수 동사로 유인했다. 비정동사 오답 두 개를 함께 넣어 정동사 여부와 수 일치를 모두 확인해야 풀 수 있게 했다.

g.passage: Eleanor Wyse keeps the bundle in a cedar box on her writing desk. The letters she discovered in the attic of her late aunt's Yorkshire farmhouse, tied with faded blue ribbon and tucked beneath a stack of unpaid tradesmen's bills, ______ a courtship conducted almost entirely through the post, one that her family never once mentioned in her presence.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "The letters"이다. 주어 뒤에 관계절과 긴 분사구가 이어지지만 그 뒤에는 정동사가 반드시 필요하다. 따라서 복수형 정동사인 D가 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 단수형이므로, 빈칸 가까이 있는 "farmhouse"나 "aunt"에 잘못 일치시킨 형태이다. B와 C는 분사형이어서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The letters." A relative clause and a long participial phrase come after it, but the sentence still needs a main (finite) verb. Choice D, a plural finite verb, is correct. Choice A is a finite verb, but it is singular, so it wrongly agrees with nearby nouns like "farmhouse" or "aunt." Choices B and C are participles, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb and make it a fragment.
g.design: 주어와 빈칸 사이에 긴 수식어구를 넣었다. 그래서 학생은 문장에 정동사가 필요한지 확인하는 것과 복수 주어에 일치시키는 것, 두 가지를 판단해야 한다. 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사가 단수형 동사를 고르도록 유인한다.

g.passage: In the salt marshes of Georgia's Sapelo Island, the burrows dug by fiddler crabs do more than shelter the animals. According to ecologists studying the marsh, the network of tunnels beneath each square meter of mud, which can extend several centimeters below the surface and fill with seawater at every high tide, ______ oxygen into otherwise stagnant sediment, helping the roots of cordgrass grow more vigorously.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸에는 주어 "the network"에 대응하는 정동사가 필요하며, 주어가 단수이므로 단수 동사 A "channels"가 정답이다. B "channel"은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "tunnels"나 관계절 속 "burrows"에 끌려 고른 복수형으로, 단수 주어 "network"와 일치하지 않는다. C "channeling"은 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되고, 지문을 훑어 읽으면 관계절의 동사 "can extend"와 "fill"을 주절 동사로 착각해 고르기 쉽다. D "to channel"도 부정사여서 주절에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs a main verb for the subject "the network," and because that subject is singular, the singular verb in A, "channels," is correct. B, "channel," is a finite verb, but it's the plural form. You might pick it if you match it to the nearby plural nouns "tunnels" or "burrows," but it doesn't agree with the singular subject "network." C, "channeling," is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb. It's easy to choose if you skim and mistake "can extend" and "fill" for main verbs, but they belong to the relative clause. D, "to channel," is an infinitive, so it also leaves the main clause without a finite verb.
g.design: To find the subject, students have to look past a long relative clause and a prepositional phrase. Then they must check both that the verb is finite (not a participle or infinitive) and that it agrees with the singular subject. Nearby plural nouns serve as distractors.

g.passage: In the decades after 1870, the network of lending libraries that sprang up in mill towns across northern England ______ factory workers with access to books they could never have afforded to buy, and historians now credit these modest institutions with fueling a marked rise in working-class literacy.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: The singular subject "network" is separated from the verb by a long modifier containing the plural nouns "libraries" and "towns." Students must also confirm that the clause needs a finite verb in the past tense to match "In the decades after 1870."
g.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 "network"이고, 빈칸 앞의 "of lending libraries that sprang up in mill towns..."는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 또한 "In the decades after 1870"이 과거 시점을 나타내므로 단수·과거형 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A는 과거 진행형이라 시제는 맞지만 "were"가 복수형이어서 가까이 있는 "libraries"나 "towns"에 잘못 일치시켰다. C는 정동사이긴 하지만 "have"가 복수형이고, 현재완료는 과거의 특정 시기와도 맞지 않는다. D는 분사여서 이 절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "network." The phrase "of lending libraries that sprang up in mill towns..." only modifies that subject. Because "In the decades after 1870" sets the sentence in a specific past period, you need a singular, past-tense finite verb, so B is correct. A is a past progressive, so its tense works, but "were" is plural and wrongly agrees with the nearby nouns "libraries" or "towns." C is a finite verb, but "have" is plural, and the present perfect doesn't fit a specific past period. D is a participle, which leaves the clause without a main verb, so the sentence doesn't hold together.

g.passage: In the 1930s, engineers building the Hoover Dam faced a problem that threatened the entire project: as the massive concrete blocks cured, the chemical reactions inside them released so much heat that, left alone, the dam would have taken more than a century to cool. Their solution, a network of steel pipes embedded in the concrete and carrying chilled river water through each block, ______ the cooling process to less than two years.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 주어 'Their solution'과 동사 사이에 긴 동격 삽입구(내부에 분사 'carrying' 포함)를 넣어, 동사가 이미 나온 것처럼 착각하게 했다. 오답은 모두 비정동사(분사·완료분사·관계절)로, 수식어로는 그럴듯하지만 주절 동사를 제공하지 못한다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'Their solution'이고, 콤마 사이의 'a network of steel pipes ... through each block'은 주어를 설명하는 동격 삽입구다. 따라서 빈칸에는 주어에 대응하는 정동사가 들어가야 하며, 과거 시제 정동사인 C가 정답이다. A의 'shortening'과 B의 'having shortened'는 분사 형태라서 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. D의 'which shortened'는 관계절을 만들어 주어를 또 수식할 뿐이어서 역시 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다. 삽입구 안의 'embedded'와 'carrying'도 분사라서 본동사가 될 수 없다는 점에 주의해야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "Their solution," and the part between the commas ("a network of steel pipes ... through each block") is an appositive that describes that subject. That means the blank needs a finite main verb to go with the subject, and the past-tense verb in C does exactly that. A ("shortening") and B ("having shortened") are participles, so they can't act as the main verb, and the sentence would be left without one. D ("which shortened") starts a relative clause that just modifies the subject again, so the sentence still has no main verb. Watch out: "embedded" and "carrying" inside the appositive are participles too, so neither one can be the main verb.

g.passage: Unlike the seeds of most flowering plants, the seeds of nearly every orchid species, which are as fine as dust and carry almost no stored food reserves, ______ on soil fungi to supply the sugars needed for germination. Botanist Hanne Rasmussen has shown that without such a fungal partner, an orchid seed may lie dormant in the ground for years.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the seeds'(복수)이고, 'of nearly every orchid species'와 which 관계절은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 D 'depend'가 정답이다. A 'depends'와 C 'has depended'는 정동사이긴 하지만 단수형이라, 가까이 있는 'species'나 'reserves'가 아닌 'seeds'와 수가 맞지 않는다. B 'depending'은 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the seeds," which is plural. The phrase "of nearly every orchid species" and the "which" clause only modify that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, and that makes D, "depend," correct. A ("depends") and C ("has depended") are finite verbs, but both are singular. They might seem right if you match the verb to a nearby word like "species," but they don't agree with "seeds." B ("depending") is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장은 장소를 나타내는 전치사구가 앞에 나오는 도치 구문이므로 주어는 빈칸 뒤의 단수 명사 'a crumbling stone chapel'이다. 따라서 주절에는 단수 정동사가 필요하고, A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이지만 가까이 있는 복수 명사 'yews'나 'sons'에 일치시킨 복수형이라 주어와 맞지 않는다. D도 복수형 'have'를 써서 같은 일치 오류가 있다. C는 분사이므로 주절에 정동사가 없어 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: This sentence uses inversion: it begins with prepositional phrases of place, and the subject, the singular noun "a crumbling stone chapel," comes after the blank. So the main clause needs a singular finite verb, which makes A correct. B is a finite verb, but its plural form agrees with nearby plural nouns like "yews" or "sons" instead of the subject. D uses the plural "have" and makes the same agreement error. C is a participle, which leaves the main clause without a finite verb, so the sentence is incomplete.

g.passage: In the salt marshes of Georgia's Sapelo Island, the burrowing activity of fiddler crabs loosens compacted mud and lets oxygen reach plant roots. A survey led by ecologist Mara Okafor found that the stretches of marsh where crab burrows were densest, despite receiving no more rainfall or sediment than neighboring plots, ______ noticeably taller stands of cordgrass by the end of each growing season.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 "the stretches of marsh"(복수)에 대한 정동사 자리이다. 관계절(where…densest)과 삽입구(despite…plots)가 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓았으므로, 주어를 정확히 찾아야 한다. B의 "produced"는 수 구분이 없는 과거형 정동사이고 found와 시제도 맞으므로 정답이다. A는 정동사이지만 단수형 was가 바로 앞의 단수 명사 marsh나 plots가 아닌 복수 주어 stretches와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라 that절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs the main verb for the subject of the that-clause, "the stretches of marsh," which is plural. A relative clause (where…densest) and an interrupting phrase (despite…plots) sit between that subject and its verb, so you have to track the subject carefully. B, "produced," is a finite past-tense verb that works with a plural subject and matches the past tense of "found," so it's correct. A is a finite verb, but its singular "was" agrees with the nearby word "marsh" instead of the plural subject "stretches." C and D are participles, which would leave the that-clause without a main verb, so the sentence would be incomplete.
g.design: 긴 관계절과 삽입구로 주어와 동사를 분리해 정동사 여부와 수 일치를 둘 다 판단하게 했다. 근처의 단수 명사 "marsh"가 A를 그럴듯하게 만든다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the number'이며, 그 뒤의 'of working-class children ... charities'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 단수 정동사가 필요하고, 'In the decades following ... 1870'이라는 과거 시점과도 맞아야 하므로 C의 'rose'가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제는 맞지만 복수형이라 단수 주어 'number'와 일치하지 않는다. 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'charities'나 'children'에 이끌리면 고르기 쉬운 오답이다. B도 복수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않고, D는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the number." Everything from "of working-class children" to "charities" is a long modifier describing that subject. So the blank needs a singular finite verb that also fits the past time frame set by "In the decades following... 1870," which makes C, "rose," correct. A uses the right tense, but "were" is plural and doesn't agree with "number." It's easy to pick if you match the verb to the nearby plural nouns "children" or "charities." B is also plural, so it doesn't agree with the subject either. D is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 수식어구와 복수 명사들(children, charities)이 단수 주어 'number'와 동사 사이에 들어가 있다. 따라서 주어-동사 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단해야 하며, A와 B는 시제가 그럴듯하지만 수가 맞지 않아 배제된다.

g.passage: In the 1880s, engineers building the Forth Bridge in Scotland faced a problem: the rail crossing had to span two deep channels of the Firth of Forth without the support of temporary scaffolding. Their solution, a series of massive steel cantilevers that ______ outward from three central towers, allowed each section to support itself as it was extended over the water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계절 안에 있으므로 that을 주어로 받는 정동사가 필요하다. 문장의 주절 동사는 뒤의 allowed이고, 관계절 "that ___ outward from three central towers"는 cantilevers를 수식하므로 정동사 extended(D)가 맞다. A의 extending과 B의 to extend는 정동사가 아니어서 that 관계절에 동사가 없게 된다. C는 that이 이미 관계절의 주어인데 주어 it을 또 넣어 주어가 중복된다.
g.explanation_en: The blank sits inside a relative clause introduced by "that," so it needs a finite verb with "that" as its subject. The main verb of the sentence is "allowed," which comes later, while the clause "that ___ outward from three central towers" describes "cantilevers," so the finite verb "extended" (D) is correct. Choices A ("extending") and B ("to extend") aren't finite verbs, which leaves the "that" clause with no verb. Choice C adds the subject "it" even though "that" is already the subject of the clause, so the clause ends up with two subjects.
g.design: 긴 동격 주어 속 관계절 안에 빈칸을 두고 주절 동사 allowed를 뒤에 배치해, 관계절에도 정동사가 필요하다는 구조 파악과 주어 중복 여부 확인의 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.

g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The islands'이고, 삽입된 관계사절 'many of which began as termite mounds colonized by trees' 뒤에 문장의 본동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사 B('play')가 정답이다. C('plays')는 정동사이지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'trees'가 아닌 'mounds/delta' 등 단수처럼 보이는 수식어에 이끌린 단수형으로, 복수 주어 'islands'와 일치하지 않는다. A('playing')와 D('having played')는 분사형이어서 문장에 본동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The islands," and after the interrupting clause "many of which began as termite mounds colonized by trees," the sentence still needs its main verb. So B ("play") is correct, because it is a finite verb that agrees with the plural subject. C ("plays") is a finite verb, but it is singular. It might seem right if you match it to a nearby noun, but it doesn't agree with the plural subject "islands." A ("playing") and D ("having played") are participles, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb and would be incomplete.
g.design: 긴 비제한 관계사절을 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입해 주어-동사 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단하게 했으며, 단수형 오답과 분사형 오답 두 개로 중간 난이도를 맞췄다.

g.passage: After Britain passed the Factory Act of 1833, government inspectors began visiting textile mills to check whether the new limits on child labor were being obeyed. The reports that these inspectors filed on conditions in Lancashire's mills during the 1830s and 1840s, many of them describing children who worked twelve-hour shifts beside unguarded machinery, ______ among the richest sources historians now have on early industrial labor.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'The reports'이고, 'that these inspectors filed...'와 'many of them describing...'은 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하며, 'now have'와도 어울리는 현재형 C 'remain'이 정답이다. A 'remains'는 정동사이지만 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'machinery'나 'labor'에 수를 맞춘 형태라서 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B 'remaining'과 D 'having remained'는 분사여서 주절에 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "The reports." The clause "that these inspectors filed..." and the phrase "many of them describing..." are modifiers that come between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, and the present-tense C, "remain," also fits with "now have." A, "remains," is a finite verb, but it is singular, as if it agreed with a nearby noun like "machinery," so it doesn't agree with the plural subject. B, "remaining," and D, "having remained," are participles, so they leave the main clause without a finite verb and make the sentence incomplete.
g.design: 긴 관계절과 독립분사구가 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓아 단수 명사에 끌려 A를 고르도록 유도했고, 분사형 두 개로 정동사 판단을 함께 요구했다.

g.passage: In the 1930s, engineers designing the Hoover Dam faced a problem: if the enormous volume of concrete were poured as a single mass, the heat released as it hardened would take more than a century to dissipate, cracking the structure as it cooled unevenly. Their solution, a network of steel pipes threaded through hundreds of separate interlocking concrete blocks and carrying chilled river water, ______ the curing time to less than two years.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'Their solution'이며, 콤마 사이의 동격구(a network ... water)를 지나면 이 주어에 대한 정동사가 필요하다. D의 'reduced'는 단수 주어와 맞는 과거 시제 정동사이므로 정답이다. A의 'reducing'과 C의 'having reduced'는 분사형이라 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 불완전한 문장이 된다. B의 'were reducing'은 정동사이지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'blocks'나 'pipes'에 끌린 복수형으로, 단수 주어 'solution'과 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun "Their solution." Once you skip over the appositive set off by commas ("a network ... river water"), you can see that this subject still needs a main verb. D, "reduced," is a past-tense main verb that works with a singular subject, so it's correct. A, "reducing," and C, "having reduced," are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb and is incomplete. B, "were reducing," is a main verb, but it's plural. It seems to agree with nearby plural nouns like "blocks" or "pipes," but it doesn't agree with the actual singular subject, "solution."
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어구 안에 복수 명사를 넣어 주어를 가렸다. 그래서 정동사인지 분사인지 판단하고, 수 일치까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.
